questions.q: Mesopotamia is the land between the Tigris and the ______ rivers.
questions.e: Mesopotamia, in present-day Iraq, lies between the Euphrates and the Tigris; the name means 'land between rivers'.

questions.q: The Mesopotamian script, written by pressing a sharpened reed into wet clay tablets, is called ______.
questions.e: Cuneiform (from Latin cuneus, wedge) consisted of wedge-shaped signs pressed into clay with a reed stylus.

questions.q: The earliest Mesopotamian tablets, written around 3200 BCE and listing goods such as oxen, fish and bread loaves, come from the temples of which southern city?
questions.e: The first tablets, about 3200 BCE, were lists of goods brought into or given out from the temples of Uruk; writing began as record-keeping.

questions.q: The famous Mesopotamian epic is about a king of Uruk who, after the death of his friend Enkidu, set out in search of immortality. Name the king.
questions.e: The Epic of Gilgamesh ends with Gilgamesh returning to Uruk and taking consolation in the city his people had built.

questions.q: The king of Akkad who, around 2370 BCE, brought northern and southern Mesopotamia under a single rule was ______.
questions.e: Sargon of Akkad is remembered as one of the first rulers to unite the whole of Mesopotamia.

questions.q: Mesopotamian mathematics was based on the number 60. Following this system, how many minutes do we still count in an hour?
questions.e: The Mesopotamian sexagesimal system survives in our 60-minute hour, 60-second minute and 360-degree circle.

questions.q: Assurbanipal (668-627 BCE), the last great Assyrian king, collected a library of clay tablets on history, epics, omens and medicine. Later, Babylon became independent again.
p: (a) In which Assyrian capital city did Assurbanipal build his library?
Nineveh
(b) Which Chaldaean ruler freed Babylonia from Assyrian rule in 625 BCE?
Nabopolassar
(c) Who was the last ruler of independent Babylon (556-539 BCE), known for collecting ancient objects?
Nabonidus
questions.e: Assurbanipal's library was at Nineveh; Nabopolassar freed Babylonia in 625 BCE, and Nabonidus was its last independent ruler before the Persian conquest.

questions.q: The first Roman emperor, whose rule from 27 BCE is called the Principate, was ______.
questions.e: Augustus founded the Principate in 27 BCE, ruling as 'first citizen' while holding real power.

questions.q: Emperor Constantine founded a second capital, ______, at the site of the old Greek town of Byzantium.
questions.e: Constantinople (modern Istanbul) was built by Constantine on the site of Byzantium and became the capital of the eastern empire.

questions.q: Rome's main rival to the east, ruled from the third century CE by the Sasanian dynasty, was ______.
questions.e: The Sasanians of Iran were Rome's chief rival power in the east and fought several wars with it.

questions.q: Constantine introduced a new gold coin containing 4.5 gm of pure gold. It was called the ______.
questions.e: The solidus was minted in millions and stayed a stable currency long after the Roman empire in the west ended.

questions.q: Wine, olive oil and other liquids were transported across the Roman empire in large containers called ______.
questions.e: Fragments of amphorae, such as those at Monte Testaccio in Rome, help historians trace Roman trade in wine and olive oil.

questions.q: The emperor (284-305) who gave up territories of little value, fortified the frontiers and separated civil from military functions was ______.
questions.e: Diocletian reorganised provincial boundaries and separated civil and military authority, reforms continued by Constantine.

questions.q: The Roman empire covered parts of Europe, West Asia and North Africa and was culturally very diverse, yet its government used only two main languages.
p: (a) Which language was used for administration in the eastern half of the empire?
Greek
(b) Which language was used for administration in the western half?
Latin
(c) Name the body of the aristocracy that had existed since the days of the Republic and continued under the emperors.
Senate|the Senate|Roman Senate
questions.e: Greek dominated the east and Latin the west; the Senate, a body of wealthy aristocrats, survived from the Republic into the imperial period.

questions.q: Genghis Khan was born around 1162 with the name ______.
questions.e: Temujin took the title Genghis Khan, 'Oceanic Khan' or 'Universal Ruler', in 1206.

questions.q: The code of law of the Mongols, said to have been laid down by Genghis Khan, was called the ______.
questions.e: The yasa was a collection of rules and customs that held the Mongol tribes together and gave them a shared identity.

questions.q: In 1206 Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan at an assembly of Mongol chiefs called a ______.
questions.e: The quriltai was the assembly of Mongol chiefs that took major decisions, including the choice of the Great Khan.

questions.q: The fast courier system of the Mongols, with fresh horses and riders at fixed posts, was called ______.
questions.e: The yam linked distant parts of the Mongol empire; it was financed by a contribution from nomads of a tenth of their herds.

questions.q: The grandson of Genghis Khan who founded the Yuan dynasty in China was ______.
questions.e: Qubilai Khan conquered China and founded the Yuan dynasty; Hulegu ruled Iran and Batu the Golden Horde.

questions.q: Genghis Khan organised his army in decimal units. The largest unit, of 10,000 soldiers, was called a ______.
questions.e: Units of 10 (arban), 100 (jaghun), 1,000 (minqan) and 10,000 (tumen) mixed different tribes, breaking old tribal loyalties.

questions.q: In medieval French society, the first order consisted of the ______.
questions.e: Society was divided into three orders: the clergy (first), the nobility (second) and the peasantry (third).

questions.q: The Church's right to collect one-tenth of the produce of peasants was called the ______.
questions.e: The tithe was a tax of one-tenth of agricultural produce paid to the Church; the taille was a direct tax paid to the king.

questions.q: A lord's estate, with his house, his private fields and pastures and the village of his tenants, was called a ______.
questions.e: The manor was nearly self-sufficient, producing its own food, cloth and tools, with the lord's house at its centre.

questions.q: A famous Benedictine monastery, founded in 910 in Burgundy in central France, was at ______.
questions.e: The monastery of Cluny, founded in 910, led a movement to reform monastic life and grew very wealthy and powerful.

questions.q: In the thirteenth century some monks, called friars, moved from place to place preaching and living on charity. The two orders of friars were the Franciscans and the ______.
questions.e: Franciscans and Dominicans chose to wander and preach instead of living in monasteries; Benedictines and Cistercians were monastic orders.

questions.q: The word 'feudalism' comes from the German word 'feud'. What does 'feud' mean?
questions.a: a piece of land|piece of land|land
questions.e: Feudalism describes the relationship around land: lords granted land to vassals and peasants in return for service and labour.

questions.q: The Italian artist who painted the 'Mona Lisa' and 'The Last Supper' was ______.
questions.e: Leonardo da Vinci was also deeply interested in botany, anatomy, mathematics and even tried to design a flying machine.

questions.q: The Swiss historian who wrote 'The Civilisation of the Renaissance in Italy' (1860) was ______.
questions.e: Burckhardt argued that Renaissance Italy saw the rise of 'humanist' culture and of the individual.

questions.q: In 1455, about 150 copies of the Bible were printed in the workshop of Johannes Gutenberg in the German city of ______.
questions.e: Gutenberg's workshop at Mainz printed the Bible with movable type; printing spread ideas of humanism rapidly across Europe.

questions.q: A German monk launched a campaign against the Catholic Church's practice of selling documents that claimed to free people from punishment for their sins. His protest started the Protestant Reformation.
p: (a) Name the monk.
Martin Luther|Luther
(b) In which year did he begin this campaign?
(c) What were the documents sold by the Church called?
indulgences|indulgence
questions.e: Martin Luther attacked the sale of indulgences in 1517, arguing that faith alone could bring salvation; this began the Protestant Reformation.

questions.q: The Polish scientist who declared that the earth and the planets revolve around the sun was ______.
questions.e: Copernicus overturned the Ptolemaic idea that the earth was the centre of the universe; Kepler and Galileo later supported his view.

questions.q: The Florentine writer of 'The Prince' (1513), who wrote that all men are bad and ever ready to display their vicious nature, was ______.
questions.e: Machiavelli's 'The Prince' discussed how a ruler should act to keep power, based on his view of human nature.

questions.q: The indigenous people of Australia are called ______.
questions.e: The Aborigines lived in Australia for over 40,000 years before the arrival of Europeans.

questions.q: The British explorer who reached Botany Bay in Australia in 1770 was ______.
questions.e: Captain James Cook reached Botany Bay in 1770 and claimed the land for Britain; a penal colony followed in 1788.

questions.q: In 1803 the USA bought the huge territory of Louisiana from ______.
questions.e: The Louisiana Purchase from France doubled the size of the USA and pushed settlers westward into Native American lands.

questions.q: The forced removal of the Cherokee from their homeland to the west in 1838-39, in which thousands died, is remembered as the ______.
questions.e: Under the US policy of Indian removal, about 15,000 Cherokee were forced westward and a quarter of them died on the way.

questions.q: In 1867 the USA purchased Alaska from ______.
questions.e: The USA bought Alaska from Russia in 1867, extending its territory to the Pacific north-west.

questions.q: When the British colonised Australia they declared it 'terra nullius'. What did this term mean?
questions.a: empty land|belonging to no one|no one's land|nobody's land|land belonging to no one
questions.e: By calling Australia terra nullius, the British refused to recognise Aboriginal ownership and took the land without treaties.

questions.q: In 1868 the Tokugawa shogunate was overthrown and the emperor was restored to power, taking the title ______.
questions.e: Emperor Mutsuhito took the title Meiji, 'enlightened rule'; the period is called the Meiji Restoration.

questions.q: During the Meiji Restoration the capital Edo was renamed ______.
questions.e: Edo was renamed Tokyo, meaning 'eastern capital', in 1868.

questions.q: The American commodore who arrived in Japan in 1853 and forced it to open its ports to trade was ______.
questions.e: Commodore Perry's arrival in 1853 led to the Treaty of Kanagawa (1854), ending Japan's isolation.

questions.q: The American occupation of Japan after its defeat in 1945 was led by General ______.
questions.e: Under MacArthur, Japan was demilitarised and a new constitution, with Article 9 renouncing war, came into force.

questions.q: Japan modernised rapidly after 1868 and recovered quickly after its defeat in the Second World War.
p: (a) The Meiji Constitution of 1889 was modelled mainly on the constitution of which country?
Germany|German|Prussia
(b) In which year did Tokyo host the Olympic Games, showing Japan's post-war recovery?
(c) What is the Japanese name of the high-speed 'bullet' trains started that same year?
Shinkansen
questions.e: The 1889 constitution followed the German model; the 1964 Tokyo Olympics and the Shinkansen symbolised Japan's economic recovery.

questions.q: Large business families in Meiji Japan, such as Mitsubishi and Sumitomo, which controlled huge business organisations, were called ______.
questions.e: The zaibatsu dominated Japan's economy until they were broken up during the American occupation after 1945.

questions.q: The People's Republic of China was established in ______.
questions.e: The Chinese Communist Party under Mao Zedong defeated the Guomindang and set up the People's Republic of China in 1949.

questions.q: The founder of the Guomindang, regarded as the founder of modern China, was ______.
questions.a: Sun Yat-sen|Sun Yatsen|Sun Yat Sen|Sun Zhongshan
questions.e: Sun Yat-sen led the 1911 revolution that overthrew the Manchu empire and set out the Three Principles of nationalism, democracy and socialism.

questions.q: The first Opium War (1839-42) was fought between China and ______.
questions.e: Britain fought China to keep its profitable opium trade; China's defeat led to the Treaty of Nanjing and the loss of Hong Kong.

questions.q: In 1934-35 the Communists, led by Mao Zedong, made the Long March to ______ in north-western China.
questions.e: The Long March of about 6,000 miles took the Communists to Yan'an, where they built their base.

questions.q: On 4 May 1919 students protested in China against the decisions of the peace conference held after the First World War.
p: (a) In which city did the May Fourth protest begin?
Beijing|Peking
(b) Name the peace conference whose decision they protested against.
Paris Peace Conference|Versailles|Paris|Treaty of Versailles|Versailles Peace Conference
(c) Which Chinese territory, earlier held by Germany, was given to Japan?
Shandong|Shantung
questions.e: The Paris Peace Conference handed Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan; Beijing students protested, starting the May Fourth Movement.

questions.q: After the Communist victory in 1949, China and Taiwan followed different paths.
p: (a) To which island did Chiang Kai-shek and the Guomindang flee after 1949?
Taiwan|Formosa
(b) Which leader began economic reforms and the 'open door' policy in China from 1978?
Deng Xiaoping|Deng
(c) In which year did Taiwan become a Japanese colony?
questions.e: Taiwan was a Japanese colony from 1895 to 1945; Chiang Kai-shek set up the Republic of China there, while Deng Xiaoping opened China's economy from 1978.

questions.q: The first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India, often called the father of Indian archaeology, was ______.
questions.e: Cunningham, the first Director-General of the ASI, began archaeological excavations in the mid-nineteenth century; he collected Harappan seals but did not realise how old they were.

questions.q: The Great Bath, a large rectangular tank in a courtyard, was found at which Harappan site?
questions.e: The Great Bath on the Citadel at Mohenjodaro was probably used for some kind of special ritual bath.

questions.q: Evidence of a ploughed field has been found at which Harappan site in Rajasthan?
questions.e: The field at Kalibangan had two sets of furrows at right angles, suggesting two different crops were grown together.

questions.q: Which tiny Harappan settlement was almost exclusively devoted to craft production such as bead-making, shell-cutting, metal-working and seal-making?
questions.e: Chanhudaro, less than 7 hectares in area, was a specialised craft centre of the Harappan civilisation.

questions.q: In 1924 the Director-General of the ASI announced the discovery of a new civilisation in the Indus valley. The Harappans obtained raw materials from distant regions.
p: (a) Name the Director-General who made this announcement.
John Marshall|Sir John Marshall|Marshall
(b) Copper was probably brought from the Khetri region of which present-day state?
Rajasthan
(c) The Harappan settlement at Shortughai, near a source of lapis lazuli, is in which present-day country?
Afghanistan
questions.e: John Marshall announced the civilisation in 1924; Harappans sent expeditions to Khetri (Rajasthan) for copper and settled at Shortughai (Afghanistan) for lapis lazuli.

questions.q: In which year did James Prinsep decipher the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts?
questions.e: Prinsep's decipherment in 1838 made it possible to read Ashoka's inscriptions and gave a new direction to early Indian history.

questions.q: Most Ashokan inscriptions refer to him as 'devanampiya' (beloved of the gods) and ______ (pleasant to behold).
questions.e: The inscriptions called the king devanampiya piyadassi; another inscription naming Ashoka confirmed who this was.

questions.q: The early fortified capital of Magadha, the Prakrit name for present-day Rajgir, was ______.
questions.e: Rajagaha, a fort amid hills, was Magadha's capital; in the fourth century BCE the capital shifted to Pataliputra.

questions.q: The Greek ambassador who lived at the court of Chandragupta Maurya and wrote an account of it was ______.
questions.e: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus; his account, the Indica, survives in fragments quoted by later Greek writers.

questions.q: Colossal statues of Kushana rulers have been found installed in a shrine at Mat near ______ in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.e: The Kushanas projected themselves as god-like; their huge statues at Mat near Mathura show this ideal of divine kingship.

questions.q: The project to prepare a critical edition of the Mahabharata, begun in 1919, was led by the Sanskritist ______.
questions.a: V.S. Sukthankar|Sukthankar|V S Sukthankar|Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar|VS Sukthankar
questions.e: Under V.S. Sukthankar, scholars compared Sanskrit manuscripts from across India over 47 years to prepare the critical edition.

questions.q: The practice of marrying outside one's own kin group, such as one's gotra, is called ______.
questions.e: Exogamy means marriage outside the unit; Brahmanical rules required women to marry outside their father's gotra.

questions.q: Draupadi's marriage to the five Pandavas is an example of ______.
questions.e: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having several husbands; polygyny is a man having several wives.

questions.q: Satavahana rulers, such as Gotami-puta Siri-Satakani, were identified by names derived from the names of their ______.
questions.e: Such metronymics (names derived from the mother) appear in Satavahana inscriptions, though succession to the throne was usually patrilineal.

questions.q: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is located in which present-day state?
questions.e: Sanchi, near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, survived largely because the Begums of Bhopal helped preserve it.

questions.q: The Buddha gave his first sermon at ______, near Varanasi.
questions.e: The first sermon at Sarnath set the 'wheel of dharma' in motion; enlightenment was at Bodh Gaya and death at Kusinagara.

questions.q: Of the three 'baskets' of Buddhist texts (Tipitaka), the rules and regulations for those who joined the sangha were included in the ______.
questions.e: The Vinaya Pitaka had rules for monks and nuns, the Sutta Pitaka the Buddha's teachings and the Abhidhamma Pitaka philosophy.

questions.q: Followers of Mahayana Buddhism described the older Buddhist tradition as ______, the 'lesser vehicle'.
questions.e: Mahayana means 'great vehicle'; its followers called the older tradition Hinayana, while those followers called themselves Theravadins.

questions.q: Al-Biruni's book on India, written in Arabic, is called ______.
questions.a: Kitab-ul-Hind|Kitab ul Hind|Kitab-al-Hind|Kitab al Hind|Kitabul Hind
questions.e: Kitab-ul-Hind has 80 chapters on religion, philosophy, festivals, astronomy, customs, laws and more.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta's book of travels, written in Arabic, is called ______.
questions.e: The Rihla gives rich details of social and cultural life in the Delhi Sultanate in the fourteenth century.

questions.q: The French physician who travelled in Mughal India (1656-1668) and compared it unfavourably with Europe was ______.
questions.e: Bernier argued that the absence of private property in land was the crucial difference between Mughal India and Europe.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta described two Indian plants that were unfamiliar to his readers: the coconut and the ______.
questions.e: He compared the coconut to a man's head and described how paan (betel leaf) was eaten with areca nut.

questions.q: Al-Biruni (born 973) and Ibn Battuta (fourteenth century) were travellers who wrote about India.
p: (a) Al-Biruni was born in Khwarizm, in which present-day country?
Uzbekistan
(b) Which ruler invaded Khwarizm in 1017 and took Al-Biruni to his capital Ghazni?
Mahmud of Ghazni|Sultan Mahmud|Mahmud|Mahmud Ghaznavi
(c) Which Sultan of Delhi appointed Ibn Battuta as the qazi (judge) of Delhi?
Muhammad bin Tughlaq|Muhammad bin Tughluq|Muhammad Tughlaq|Muhammad Tughluq
questions.e: Al-Biruni came from Khwarizm (Uzbekistan) and was taken to Ghazni by Sultan Mahmud; Ibn Battuta served Muhammad bin Tughlaq as qazi of Delhi.

questions.q: The Tamil poet-saints devoted to Vishnu were called ______.
questions.e: The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu and the Nayanars devotees of Shiva; both travelled singing hymns in Tamil.

questions.q: The Virashaiva (Lingayat) tradition in Karnataka was started in the twelfth century by ______.
questions.e: Basavanna, a minister in a Chalukya court, led the Virashaivas, who challenged caste and worshipped Shiva as a linga.

questions.q: The Sufi saint whose dargah at Ajmer was visited by Akbar fourteen times was ______.
questions.a: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti|Muinuddin Chishti|Moinuddin Chishti|Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti|Shaikh Muinuddin Sijzi
questions.e: The dargah of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti, the 'Gharib Nawaz', at Ajmer became one of the most popular pilgrimage centres.

questions.q: Guru Nanak's compositions, along with those of his successors and others, were compiled in the Adi Granth Sahib by ______.
questions.e: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604; Guru Gobind Singh later added the compositions of Guru Tegh Bahadur.

questions.q: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 by two brothers, Harihara and ______.
questions.e: Harihara and Bukka founded the Vijayanagara empire in 1336, with its capital at Hampi.

questions.q: The ruins at Hampi were brought to light in 1800 by an engineer and antiquarian who later became the first Surveyor General of India. Name him.
questions.e: Colin Mackenzie prepared the first survey map of Hampi, using information from priests of the Virupaksha temple.

questions.q: In 1565 the Vijayanagara army led by Rama Raya was defeated by the combined forces of the Deccan sultanates at the battle of ______.
questions.e: After the defeat at Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota) in 1565 the city of Vijayanagara was sacked and abandoned.

questions.q: Vijayanagara reached the peak of its power under Krishnadeva Raya, who ruled from 1509 to 1529.
p: (a) To which dynasty did Krishnadeva Raya belong?
Tuluva
(b) What were the military chiefs who controlled forts and armed supporters called?
nayakas|nayaka|nayaks
(c) On the banks of which river was the city of Vijayanagara located?
Tungabhadra
questions.e: Krishnadeva Raya was of the Tuluva dynasty; nayakas were military chiefs, and the capital stood on the Tungabhadra river.

questions.q: The Ain-i Akbari, a major source for the agrarian history of the Mughal period, was written by ______.
questions.a: Abu'l Fazl|Abul Fazl|Abu al-Fazl|Abul Fazal|Abu'l Fazl Allami
questions.e: Abu'l Fazl, Akbar's court historian, completed the Ain-i Akbari in 1598 as part of the Akbarnama.

questions.q: The term most often used in Indo-Persian sources of the Mughal period for a peasant was ______.
questions.e: Raiyat (plural riaya) was the usual term for peasants; muzarian, kisan and asami were also used.

questions.q: In the Ain-i Akbari's classification of land, land that was cultivated every year and never left fallow was called ______.
questions.e: Polaj was cultivated annually; parauti was left fallow for a time, chachar for three or four years, and banjar for five years or more.

questions.q: Lands held by zamindars as their personal property, cultivated for their own use with hired or servile labour, were called ______.
questions.e: Zamindars could sell, bequeath or mortgage their milkiyat lands; their power also came from collecting revenue for the state.

questions.q: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal in ______.
questions.e: Under the Permanent Settlement of 1793, revenue was fixed permanently and zamindars had to pay it to the Company.

questions.q: The Governor-General under whom the Permanent Settlement was introduced was ______.
questions.e: Charles Cornwallis was Governor-General when the Permanent Settlement was introduced in 1793.

questions.q: By 1832 a large area of land in the Rajmahal hills was demarcated as the land of the Santhals. It was called the ______.
questions.e: The Damin-i-Koh was demarcated with pillars; after the Santhal revolt (1855-56) the Santhal Pargana was created.

questions.q: In 1875 peasants in parts of the Bombay Deccan rose in revolt, burning bonds and account books.
p: (a) The revolt began at the village of Supa in which district?
Poona|Pune
(b) Against whom were these attacks mainly directed?
moneylenders|moneylender|sahukars|sahukar
(c) In which year was the report of the Deccan Riots Commission presented to the British Parliament?
questions.e: The Deccan riots began at Supa in Poona district against sahukars (moneylenders); the Deccan Riots Commission's report was presented in 1878.

questions.q: The revolt of 1857 began at ______ on 10 May 1857.
questions.e: Sepoys at Meerut mutinied on 10 May 1857 and marched to Delhi the next day.

questions.q: Which kingdom was annexed by the British in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment?
questions.e: Awadh was annexed in 1856 and Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta; this fuelled the revolt there.

questions.q: In 1857 the rebels in several centres turned to members of old ruling families for leadership.
p: (a) Who, the adopted son of the Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the rebels at Kanpur?
Nana Sahib|Nana Saheb
(b) Which queen led the rebellion at Jhansi?
Rani Lakshmibai|Lakshmibai|Laxmibai|Rani Laxmibai|Lakshmi Bai
(c) Which Begum of Awadh led the uprising in Lucknow?
Begum Hazrat Mahal|Hazrat Mahal
questions.e: Nana Sahib at Kanpur, Rani Lakshmibai at Jhansi and Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow were drawn into leading the revolt.

questions.q: Rebel sepoys who reached Delhi in May 1857 declared which Mughal emperor to be their leader?
questions.a: Bahadur Shah Zafar|Bahadur Shah|Bahadur Shah II
questions.e: The aged Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed leader; after the revolt he was tried and exiled to Rangoon.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in January ______.
questions.e: Gandhi returned in January 1915 after two decades in South Africa, where he had first used satyagraha.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Gandhi's first major public appearance in India was at the opening of which university in February 1916?
questions.e: At the opening of BHU, Gandhi criticised the Indian elite for its lack of concern for the labouring poor.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Gandhi's early campaigns in India brought him into contact with peasants and workers, and his first all-India movement followed.
p: (a) In 1917 Gandhi took up the cause of indigo cultivators in which district of Bihar?
Champaran
(b) In 1918 Gandhi intervened in a dispute between mill owners and workers in which city?
Ahmedabad
(c) The Non-cooperation Movement was withdrawn in February 1922 after violence at which place?
Chauri Chaura|Chauri-Chaura
questions.e: Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad (1918) and Kheda gave Gandhi a mass base; he called off Non-cooperation after policemen were killed at Chauri Chaura.

questions.q: The Constituent Assembly of India held its first session in December ______.
questions.e: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946 and held eleven sessions over nearly three years.

questions.q: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution was ______.
questions.a: B.R. Ambedkar|Ambedkar|Dr Ambedkar|Dr B R Ambedkar|Bhimrao Ambedkar|BR Ambedkar
questions.e: Dr B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and guided the Draft Constitution through the Assembly.

questions.q: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946 by ______.
questions.e: Nehru's Objectives Resolution declared India an 'Independent Sovereign Republic' and set out the ideals of the Constitution.

questions.q: The Constituent Assembly completed its work in about three years.
p: (a) The Constitution came into effect on 26 January of which year?
(b) Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
Rajendra Prasad|Dr Rajendra Prasad
(c) In which year was the Constitution adopted by the Assembly, on 26 November?
questions.e: Under its President Rajendra Prasad, the Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: The Harappan civilisation is named after ______, the first site where this culture was discovered.
questions.e: Archaeologists name a culture after the site where it was first found; Harappa is in present-day Pakistan.

questions.q: Harappan seals were usually made of a stone called ______.
questions.e: Seals, usually of steatite, often carry an animal motif and signs of the Harappan script.

questions.q: One of the most distinctive features of Harappan cities was the carefully planned ______ system.
questions.e: Streets and houses were laid out so that covered drains could carry waste water away.

questions.q: The Mature Harappan culture is dated between c. 2600 BCE and c. ______ BCE.
questions.e: NCERT dates the Mature Harappan culture to c. 2600-1900 BCE.

questions.q: In which direction was the Harappan script written?
questions.a: right to left|from right to left
questions.e: Some seals show wider spacing on the right and cramped signs on the left, showing the engraver began on the right.

questions.q: Nageshwar and Balakot, both near the coast, were specialised centres for making objects of ______, such as bangles, ladles and inlay.
questions.e: Finished shell objects were then taken to the large urban centres.

questions.q: The Harappans may have sent expeditions to the ______ region of Rajasthan for copper.
questions.e: Expeditions went to areas such as Khetri (for copper) and south India (for gold).

questions.q: Mesopotamian texts mention contact with a region called ______, probably the Harappan region.
questions.e: Meluhha is described as a land of seafarers; Dilmun and Magan were other regions in the Gulf area.

questions.q: At Mohenjodaro, the smaller but higher part of the settlement, on the west, is called the ______.
questions.e: The settlement was divided into the Citadel and the larger but lower Lower Town.

questions.q: Harappan weights were usually cubical, with no markings, and were made of a stone called ______.
questions.e: The lower denominations of weights were binary (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and so on).

questions.q: Harappan bricks were of a standardised ratio: the length was how many times the height?
questions.e: The length and breadth of bricks were four times and twice the height respectively.

questions.q: In the early twentieth century, Harappan seals were found at two sites by officers of the Archaeological Survey of India.
p: (a) Who found seals at Harappa?
Daya Ram Sahni|Dayaram Sahni|Sahni
(b) Who found similar seals at Mohenjodaro?
Rakhal Das Banerji|R.D. Banerji|Banerji|Rakhaldas Banerjee|Banerjee
questions.e: Daya Ram Sahni found seals at Harappa and Rakhal Das Banerji found similar seals at Mohenjodaro, which showed they belonged to one culture.

questions.q: Early Buddhist and Jaina texts mention how many states known as mahajanapadas?
questions.e: The sixteen mahajanapadas included Vajji, Magadha, Koshala, Kuru, Panchala, Gandhara and Avanti.

questions.q: Which mahajanapada became the most powerful between the sixth and the fourth centuries BCE?
questions.e: Fertile land, iron mines, elephants and the Ganga and its tributaries helped Magadha grow.

questions.q: The capital of the Mauryan empire was ______.
questions.e: Pataliputra is near present-day Patna in Bihar.

questions.q: The Mauryan empire was founded around 321 BCE by ______.
questions.e: Chandragupta Maurya was the grandfather of Ashoka.

questions.q: The text on statecraft traditionally ascribed to Kautilya (Chanakya) is the ______.
questions.e: Parts of the Arthashastra are believed to have been composed by Kautilya, the minister of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.q: Ashokan inscriptions in the north-west of the subcontinent were written in the ______ script.
questions.e: Most other Ashokan inscriptions were in the Brahmi script.

questions.q: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), in praise of Samudragupta, was composed by his court poet ______.
questions.e: Prashastis were composed in Sanskrit in praise of the ruler.

questions.q: According to Sangam texts, the three chiefdoms of Tamilakam were the Cholas, the Pandyas and the ______.
questions.e: These chiefdoms emerged in Tamilakam, the ancient Tamil country.

questions.q: Ashoka appointed special officers, known as ______, to spread the message of dhamma.
questions.a: dhamma mahamatta|dhamma mahamattas|dhamma mahamatra|dhamma mahamatras|dharma mahamatra|dharma mahamatras
questions.e: Ashoka believed that he could ensure the well-being of people through dhamma.

questions.q: The earliest coins, made of silver and copper and used from c. sixth century BCE, are called ______ coins.
questions.e: They were punched with symbols and have been found at many sites across the subcontinent.

questions.q: The first gold coins in the subcontinent were issued in c. first century CE by the ______.
questions.e: Kushana gold coins were almost identical in weight to those of the contemporary Roman emperors and the Parthian rulers of Iran.

questions.q: Besides the capital at Pataliputra, the Mauryan empire had several provincial centres.
p: (a) Which provincial centre was in present-day Odisha?
Tosali
(b) Which provincial centre was in present-day Karnataka?
Suvarnagiri
questions.e: The five major political centres were Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjayini, Tosali and Suvarnagiri, all mentioned in Ashokan inscriptions.

questions.q: Marriage within a unit, such as a kin group, caste or a group living in the same locality, is called ______.
questions.e: Exogamy, by contrast, is marriage outside the unit.

questions.q: The practice of a man having several wives is called ______.
questions.e: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having several husbands.

questions.q: The Mahabharata is traditionally believed to have been composed by the sage ______.
questions.e: According to tradition Vyasa composed the epic, which was written down by Ganesha.

questions.q: Tracing descent from father to son, grandson and so on is called ______.
questions.e: Matriliny is the tracing of descent through the mother.

questions.q: According to the Manusmriti, the wealth a woman received at the time of her marriage, which she could keep, was called ______.
questions.e: Her children could inherit it, without any claim from her husband.

questions.q: According to Brahmanical practice, every Brahmana man and woman belonged to a ______, named after a Vedic seer.
questions.e: Women were expected to give up their father's gotra and adopt that of their husband on marriage.

questions.q: The Manusmriti was compiled between c. 200 BCE and ______ CE.
questions.e: The Manusmriti is one of the best known Dharmashastras.

questions.q: The Brahmanas classified some people, who handled corpses and dead animals, as "untouchable" and placed them at the very bottom of the social order. They were called ______.
questions.e: The Manusmriti laid down that chandalas had to live outside the village.

questions.q: According to the Purusha sukta of the Rigveda, the four varnas emerged from the body of ______, the primeval man.
questions.e: The Brahmanas used this verse to claim that the varna order was of divine origin.

questions.q: Ekalavya, a forest-dwelling nishada, cut off his right thumb as a fee for the teacher ______.
questions.e: Drona had earlier refused to accept Ekalavya as a pupil.

questions.q: In the Mahabharata, which mother advised Duryodhana to make peace with his cousins and not go to war?
questions.e: Duryodhana did not listen to his mother Gandhari and fought the war, in which he was defeated.

questions.q: The Shakas, who came from Central Asia, were regarded by the Brahmanas as ______, or outsiders.
questions.e: Yet a Sanskrit inscription describes the Shaka ruler Rudradaman as rebuilding the Sudarshana lake.

questions.q: The Mahabharata tells the story of one of the Pandavas who married a woman from outside the varna order.
p: (a) Whom did Bhima marry?
Hidimba|Hidimbi
(b) What was the name of their son?
Ghatotkacha|Ghatotkach
questions.e: Bhima married the rakshasini Hidimba, and their son Ghatotkacha fought on the side of the Pandavas.

questions.q: The Buddha attained enlightenment at ______.
questions.e: Siddhartha meditated under a pipal tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha, the enlightened one.

questions.q: According to Jaina tradition, Vardhamana Mahavira was the ______ tirthankara.
questions.e: He was preceded by 23 other teachers or tirthankaras.

questions.q: Buddhist monasteries, where monks lived, were called ______.
questions.e: As monks began to live permanently in one place, monasteries known as viharas were built.

questions.q: In the Tipitaka, the teachings of the Buddha were placed in the ______ Pitaka.
questions.e: The Vinaya Pitaka had rules for the sangha and the Abhidhamma Pitaka dealt with philosophy.

questions.q: The hemispherical mound of a stupa is called the ______.
questions.e: The stupa originated as a simple semi-circular mound of earth, later called anda.

questions.q: The richly carved gateways of the Great Stupa at Sanchi are called ______.
questions.e: The four gateways at Sanchi are among its most famous features.

questions.q: The Buddha's foster mother, who was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni, was ______.
questions.e: She was ordained after the Buddha's disciple Ananda persuaded the Buddha to allow women into the sangha.

questions.q: The Buddha passed away (attained mahaparinibbana) at ______.
questions.e: Kusinara was one of the places associated with the Buddha's life that became sacred.

questions.q: The Buddhist text that is a collection of verses composed by bhikkhunis is the ______.
questions.e: The Therigatha is part of the Sutta Pitaka and gives an insight into women's social and spiritual experiences.

questions.q: The rulers of Bhopal who gave money to preserve the stupa at Sanchi were Shahjehan Begum and her successor ______.
questions.a: Sultan Jehan Begum|Sultan Jahan Begum|Sultan Jehan
questions.e: Sultan Jehan Begum also funded the museum built there and the publication of John Marshall's volumes on Sanchi.

questions.q: In Mahayana Buddhism, a compassionate being who accumulated merit through his efforts but used it to help others attain nibbana was called a ______.
questions.e: The worship of images of the Buddha and of Bodhisattas became an important part of this tradition.

questions.q: Parts of a stupa had their own names.
p: (a) What was the balcony-like structure above the anda, representing the abode of the gods, called?
harmika
(b) What was the mast that arose from it, often topped by an umbrella (chhatri), called?
yashti|yasti
questions.e: Above the anda was the harmika; arising from it was the yashti, often surmounted by a chhatri; a railing separated the sacred space.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier in present-day ______.
questions.e: He belonged to a respectable family known for its experts in Islamic religious law.

questions.q: In which language did Al-Biruni write his book on India?
questions.e: His Kitab-ul-Hind is written in simple and lucid Arabic.

questions.q: Francois Bernier, who travelled in Mughal India, came from which country?
questions.e: Bernier was a French doctor, political philosopher and historian.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta reached Sind in the year ______.
questions.e: He then travelled to Delhi to the court of the Sultan.

questions.q: The Delhi Sultan who appointed Ibn Battuta as the qazi (judge) of Delhi was ______.
questions.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was impressed by his scholarship.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta described two kinds of postal system in India: the horse-post, called uluq, and the foot-post, called ______.
questions.e: The foot-post had three stations per mile, and news was carried by runners.

questions.q: Bernier dedicated his major writing to the king of France, ______.
questions.e: Many of his other works were written as letters to influential officials and philosophers.

questions.q: In India, Bernier was physician to which Mughal prince, the eldest son of Shah Jahan?
questions.e: He later became an intellectual and scientist attached to Danishmand Khan, an Armenian amir at the Mughal court.

questions.q: Al-Biruni was born in 973 in ______, in present-day Uzbekistan.
questions.e: He was taken to Ghazni when Sultan Mahmud invaded Khwarizm in 1017.

questions.q: The French philosopher who used Bernier's account to develop the idea of oriental despotism was ______.
questions.e: The idea was that in the East rulers had absolute authority over subjects who were kept in subjugation and poverty.

questions.q: In the nineteenth century, Karl Marx further developed Bernier's ideas into the concept of the ______ mode of production.
questions.e: Marx argued that in India surplus was appropriated by the state before colonialism.

questions.q: Ibn Battuta stayed in Delhi for several years before travelling further east.
p: (a) In which year was he ordered to go to China as the Sultan's envoy?
(b) To whom did he later dictate his account of his travels?
Ibn Juzayy|Ibn Juzay|Ibn Jazayy
questions.e: In 1342 Ibn Battuta set out for China as the envoy of Muhammad bin Tughlaq; back in Morocco, Ibn Juzayy wrote down what he dictated.

questions.q: The Tamil poet-saints devoted to Shiva were called ______.
questions.e: The Alvars were devoted to Vishnu and the Nayanars to Shiva.

questions.q: The Sufi hospice where a master lived with his disciples was called a ______.
questions.e: The khanqah was controlled by a teaching master known as shaikh, pir or murshid.

questions.q: The annual celebration of a Sufi saint's death anniversary, marking the union of his soul with God, is called ______.
questions.e: People believed that saints in death were nearer to God than when living.

questions.q: The disciples of a Sufi master (shaikh or pir) were called ______.
questions.e: The master enrolled disciples (murids) and appointed a successor (khalifa).

questions.q: The chain linking a Sufi master and his disciples in an unbroken spiritual line back to the Prophet Muhammad is called a ______.
questions.e: Sufi orders such as the Chishti order are called silsilas.

questions.q: The woman Alvar whose devotional compositions express her love for Vishnu was ______.
questions.e: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a devotee of Shiva.

questions.q: According to some traditions, the preceptor (guru) of Mirabai was ______, a leather worker.
questions.e: Mirabai, a Rajput princess from Merta in Marwar, became a devotee of Krishna.

questions.q: The dargah of Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya is in ______.
questions.e: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya was a Chishti master; Amir Khusrau was among his disciples.

questions.q: The compositions of the twelve Alvars were compiled into an anthology called the ______.
questions.e: The anthology was compiled by the tenth century and was described as the Tamil Veda.

questions.q: The Sufi practice of listening to music and mystical chants to evoke divine ecstasy is called ______.
questions.e: Sama was an important part of Chishti practice.

questions.q: Among the Virashaivas (Lingayats), a wandering monk was called a ______.
questions.e: Lingayats worship Shiva in his manifestation as a linga.

questions.q: The collection of Kabir's verses preserved by the Kabirpanth in Varanasi and elsewhere in Uttar Pradesh is the ______.
questions.e: The Kabir Granthavali is associated with the Dadupanth in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Guru Nanak founded a tradition whose scripture grew over time.
p: (a) In which year was Guru Nanak born?
(b) Which Guru added the compositions of Guru Tegh Bahadur and called the scripture the Guru Granth Sahib?
Guru Gobind Singh|Gobind Singh|Guru Govind Singh
questions.e: Guru Nanak was born in 1469; the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, included the ninth Guru's compositions and named the scripture the Guru Granth Sahib.

questions.q: The ruins of Vijayanagara, in present-day Karnataka, are now known as ______.
questions.e: The name Hampi is derived from Pampadevi, the local mother goddess.

questions.q: The guardian deity of the Vijayanagara kingdom, a form of Shiva, was ______.
questions.e: Royal orders were signed in the name of Shri Virupaksha.

questions.q: The first dynasty to rule Vijayanagara was the ______ dynasty.
questions.e: The Sangama dynasty ruled till 1485; it was followed by the Saluvas, Tuluvas and Aravidus.

questions.q: Krishnadeva Raya wrote a work on statecraft in Telugu called the ______.
questions.e: In it he advised the king on ports, commerce and the welfare of subjects.

questions.q: The ambassador sent by the ruler of Persia who visited Vijayanagara in the fifteenth century and was impressed by its fortifications was ______.
questions.e: He described the city as having seven lines of forts.

questions.q: Abdur Razzaq wrote that Vijayanagara was encircled by how many lines of forts?
questions.e: The fort walls enclosed not only the city but also its agricultural hinterland and forests.

questions.q: Rituals associated with which festival were performed on the massive platform in the royal centre known as the dibba?
questions.e: The Mahanavami festival was held over nine days in the autumn months.

questions.q: The most important tank of Vijayanagara, built in the early years of the fifteenth century, was the ______ tank.
questions.e: Water from this tank irrigated nearby fields and was led by a channel to the royal centre.

questions.q: The towering gateways of Vijayanagara temples, which signalled the presence of the temple from a great distance, were called ______.
questions.e: They often dwarfed the towers on the central shrines.

questions.q: Which Vijayanagara temple has a chariot made of stone in its courtyard?
questions.e: The principal deity, Vitthala, is a form of Vishnu worshipped in Maharashtra.

questions.q: The Portuguese visitor who described the city of Vijayanagara and Krishnadeva Raya in the sixteenth century was Domingo ______.
questions.e: Domingo Paes described the city as being as large as Rome.

questions.q: The Rayas were called narapati (lord of men) and the Deccan Sultans ashvapati (lord of horses). The ruling lineage of Orissa was called ______ (lord of elephants).
questions.e: These titles appear in the popular traditions of Vijayanagara.

questions.q: Vijayanagara was sacked after the battle of 1565, but the empire continued.
p: (a) Which dynasty ruled after 1565?
Aravidu|Aravidus
(b) From which city did it rule at first?
Penukonda
questions.e: The Aravidu dynasty ruled from Penukonda and later from Chandragiri, near Tirupati.

questions.q: In Mughal sources, the autumn cropping season is called ______.
questions.e: Agriculture was organised around the kharif (autumn) and rabi (spring) seasons.

questions.q: The Ain-i Akbari was completed in the year ______.
questions.e: It was completed in the forty-second regnal year of Akbar.

questions.q: Abu'l Fazl wrote the Ain-i Akbari during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
questions.e: The Ain was part of a larger history of Akbar's reign, the Akbar Nama.

questions.q: Peasants who lived in the village in which they held their land were called ______.
questions.e: Non-resident cultivators who cultivated land elsewhere were called pahi-kashta.

questions.q: Non-resident cultivators who belonged to some other village but cultivated land elsewhere were called ______.
questions.e: Some moved by choice, for better terms of revenue, and some were forced to by famine.

questions.q: The headman of the village panchayat was known as the muqaddam or ______.
questions.e: Headmen were chosen through the consensus of village elders.

questions.q: In the Ain-i Akbari, land left out of cultivation for a time so that it could recover its strength was called ______.
questions.e: Chachar was land fallow for three or four years and banjar for five years or more.

questions.q: Mughal sources call cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane ______, meaning perfect crops.
questions.a: jins-i kamil|jins i kamil|jins-i-kamil|jins e kamil
questions.e: The state encouraged their cultivation as they brought in more revenue.

questions.q: In the Ain-i Akbari, land that had remained uncultivated for five years and more was called ______.
questions.e: The Ain lists four classes of land: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.

questions.q: Under the Mughals, the amount of revenue assessed was called ______, as opposed to hasil, the amount actually collected.
questions.e: Akbar ordered his revenue collectors to press for payment in cash but keep the option of payment in kind open.

questions.q: The accountant of the village panchayat in Mughal times was the ______.
questions.e: The panchayat's accounts were prepared by the accountant or patwari.

questions.q: Maize was introduced into India via Africa and ______.
questions.e: By the seventeenth century maize was listed among the major crops of western India.

questions.q: The Ain-i Akbari is part of a larger history of Akbar's reign, the Akbar Nama.
p: (a) In how many volumes was the Akbar Nama written?
(b) How many books (daftars) make up the Ain-i Akbari?
questions.e: The Akbar Nama was written in three volumes, the third being the Ain-i Akbari, which is made up of five books (daftars).

questions.q: Under the Permanent Settlement, revenue had to be paid before sunset on a specified date, or the estate could be auctioned. This was called the ______ law.
questions.e: Zamindars who failed to pay on time risked having their estates sold.

questions.q: Rich peasants in rural Bengal who acquired vast areas of land at the end of the eighteenth century were known as ______.
questions.e: Jotedars were most powerful in Dinajpur and often controlled local trade and moneylending.

questions.q: The Santhals rebelled against the colonial state in 1855-56. In which year did the rebellion begin?
questions.e: After the revolt the Santhal Pargana was created out of 5,500 square miles of the Bhagalpur and Birbhum districts.

questions.q: The Paharias, who lived around the Rajmahal hills, practised ______ cultivation.
questions.e: They cleared patches of forest by cutting bushes and burning the undergrowth.

questions.q: The Paharias are associated with the ______, while the Santhals are associated with the plough.
questions.e: The battle between the hoe and the plough was a long one between shifting cultivators and settled agriculturists.

questions.q: The surveyor employed by the East India Company who travelled through the Rajmahal hills in 1810-11 was Francis ______.
questions.e: His journals give detailed descriptions of the places he visited.

questions.q: The revenue system introduced in the Bombay Deccan in the 1820s, under which the revenue was settled directly with the ryot, was the ______ settlement.
questions.e: Each plot was surveyed and the average income from different types of soil assessed.

questions.q: The cotton boom in the Bombay Deccan in the 1860s followed the outbreak of the ______ in 1861.
questions.a: American Civil War|US Civil War|Civil War
questions.e: Cotton imports from America into Britain fell sharply, so Britain looked to India for cotton.

questions.q: The Limitation Law of 1859 stated that loan bonds signed by ryots and moneylenders would be valid for only how many years?
questions.e: Moneylenders got round it by forcing ryots to sign a new bond every three years.

questions.q: In which year were the estates of the Raja of Burdwan put up for auction, in a well-known example of the effects of the Permanent Settlement?
questions.e: Many of the buyers were the raja's own servants and agents.

questions.q: The strongmen employed by zamindars, literally "ones who wield the lathi", were called ______.
questions.e: Lathyals were used to coerce defaulting ryots.

questions.q: In 1875 ryots in the Bombay Deccan rose against moneylenders.
p: (a) In which village in Poona district did the revolt begin on 12 May 1875?
Supa
(b) In which year was the report of the Deccan Riots Commission presented to the British Parliament?
questions.e: Ryots gathered at Supa, attacked the shopkeepers and moneylenders and burnt their account books; the Commission's report was presented in 1878.

questions.q: The rebel sepoys from Meerut reached Delhi on ______ May 1857.
questions.e: They rode to Delhi the morning after the mutiny at Meerut on 10 May.

questions.q: The young soldier who was hanged for attacking his officers in Barrackpore in 1857 was ______.
questions.e: The incident at Barrackpore came before the outbreak at Meerut.

questions.q: The Nawab of Awadh who was dethroned and exiled to Calcutta when Awadh was annexed in 1856 was ______.
questions.e: The British claimed he was being removed because the region was being misgoverned.

questions.q: It was rumoured that the cartridges of the new ______ rifle were coated with the fat of cows and pigs.
questions.e: Sepoys had to bite off the paper of the cartridges before loading them.

questions.q: The subsidiary alliance was devised by ______ in 1798.
questions.e: Under it, the British kept armed forces in the territory of their allies, who paid for them.

questions.q: In Lucknow the rebels proclaimed ______, the young son of the deposed Nawab, as their leader.
questions.e: He was declared the Nawab after the fall of British authority in Lucknow.

questions.q: In 1851 Governor-General Lord Dalhousie described the kingdom of Awadh as "a ______ that will drop into our mouth one day".
questions.e: Five years later, in 1856, Awadh was annexed.

questions.q: The elderly zamindar of Arrah who led the rebellion in Bihar in 1857 was ______.
questions.a: Kunwar Singh|Kuer Singh|Kunwar Singh of Arrah
questions.e: Kunwar Singh fought the British for many months.

questions.q: The tribal cultivator who became a rebel leader of the Kols of Singhbhum in Chotanagpur in 1857 was ______.
questions.e: Local leaders like Gonoo urged people to revolt in many areas.

questions.q: The rebel leader who mobilised the headmen and cultivators of pargana Barout in Uttar Pradesh in 1857 was ______.
questions.e: Shah Mal belonged to a large village in pargana Barout and was killed in battle in July 1857.

questions.q: The British land revenue settlement introduced in Awadh in 1856, which dispossessed many taluqdars, was called the ______.
questions.e: Taluqdars lost much of their land, and many joined the revolt of 1857.

questions.q: The painting "Relief of Lucknow" (1859), celebrating the British rescue of the besieged Residency, was painted by Thomas Jones ______.
questions.e: British paintings like this glorified the British heroes who saved the English.

questions.q: During the revolt of 1857, the British Residency at Lucknow was besieged by the rebels.
p: (a) Which British Commissioner gathered the Christian population in the Residency and was killed during the siege?
Henry Lawrence|Sir Henry Lawrence|Lawrence
(b) Which begum, the mother of Birjis Qadr, played an active role in the rebellion in Lucknow?
Begum Hazrat Mahal|Hazrat Mahal
questions.e: Henry Lawrence was killed during the siege of the Residency; Begum Hazrat Mahal, mother of Birjis Qadr, took an active part in organising the uprising.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Gandhi regarded ______ as his political mentor.
questions.e: On Gokhale's advice Gandhi spent a year travelling around British India after his return.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: On 12 March 1930 Gandhi began the march to Dandi from his ashram at ______.
questions.e: The march was to break the salt law, which gave the state a monopoly on making and selling salt.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: The Quit India movement was launched in August ______.
questions.e: It began after the failure of the Cripps Mission; Gandhi was arrested at once.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: In 1919 Gandhi called for a countrywide campaign against the ______ Act, which allowed detention without trial.
questions.e: The campaign made Gandhi a truly national leader.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in April 1919 in the city of ______.
questions.e: A British Brigadier ordered his troops to open fire on a nationalist meeting.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Gandhi combined non-cooperation with the ______ movement, which sought to restore the Caliphate.
questions.e: Gandhi hoped that by joining the two movements, Hindus and Muslims would end colonial rule together.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: At the Lahore session of the Congress in December 1929, under the presidentship of ______, the goal of Purna Swaraj was declared.
questions.e: The session marked the coming of age of the younger generation in the Congress.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: "Independence Day" was first observed by the Congress on 26 January ______.
questions.e: The national flag was hoisted at different venues across the country.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 was an agreement between Gandhi and the Viceroy, Lord ______.
questions.e: Under it civil disobedience was called off and Gandhi attended the second Round Table Conference in London.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: The judge who sentenced Gandhi to six years in jail in March 1922 was Justice C.N. ______.
questions.e: The judge said he would be happy if the government later reduced the sentence.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: In which 1909 book did Gandhi criticise modern civilisation and set out his ideas on self-rule?
questions.e: Young India, Harijan and Navajivan were journals that published Gandhi's writings.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: At the end of 1946 Gandhi went to ______ in East Bengal to bring peace after communal violence.
questions.e: He walked from village to village, consoling the victims and persuading people to live together.

questions.t: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
questions.q: Provincial elections were held under the Government of India Act of 1935.
p: (a) In which year were these elections held?
(b) Out of eleven provinces, how many had a Congress "Prime Minister" after the elections?
questions.e: In the 1937 elections the Congress won a comprehensive victory; eight out of eleven provinces had a Congress Prime Minister.

questions.q: The Constitution divides subjects into three lists: the Union List, the State List and the ______ List.
questions.e: Subjects on the Concurrent List are shared by the Centre and the states.

questions.q: Which party chose to boycott the Constituent Assembly, pressing its demand for Pakistan?
questions.a: Muslim League|All India Muslim League|the Muslim League
questions.e: As a result the Assembly was dominated by the Congress.

questions.q: Gandhi felt that everyone should speak ______, a blend of Hindi and Urdu, as the national language.
questions.e: He thought it was a language easily understood by a large section of people.

questions.q: The members of the Constituent Assembly were not elected by universal franchise but by the ______ legislatures.
questions.e: The provincial legislatures had been elected in the winter of 1945-46.

questions.q: The Constitutional Advisor to the Government of India, who prepared papers on the political systems of other countries, was B.N. ______.
questions.e: B.N. Rau made a detailed study of the constitutions of other countries.

questions.q: The chief draughtsman of the Constitution, responsible for putting complex proposals into clear legal language, was S.N. ______.
questions.e: He worked closely with the Drafting Committee chaired by B.R. Ambedkar.

questions.q: The tribal leader in the Constituent Assembly who spoke for the protection of the tribes (Adivasis) was ______.
questions.e: He argued that tribes needed reserved seats in the legislature.

questions.q: The socialist and peasant leader who urged that "minorities" be interpreted in economic terms, meaning the poor and downtrodden, was ______.
questions.e: He welcomed the Objectives Resolution but stressed the need for economic justice.

questions.q: B. Pocker Bahadur of Madras made a powerful plea in the Constituent Assembly for continuing ______ electorates.
questions.e: Most nationalists opposed separate electorates, which they felt had divided people.

questions.q: The Communist member who warned that the Constituent Assembly was working under the shadow of British imperialism was ______.
questions.e: He urged members to free themselves from the influence of imperial power.

questions.q: The member from Madras who argued that the states should be strengthened, including in their financial powers, was K. ______.
questions.e: He felt that a centre burdened with too many responsibilities could not function effectively.

questions.q: The Constituent Assembly worked for about three years.
p: (a) Over how many sessions were its discussions spread?
(b) Over how many days of sittings were they spread?
questions.e: The Assembly's discussions were spread over eleven sessions, with sittings spread over 165 days.
